EdgeForge Studio — Current-State UX Walkthrough

First-hand capture of the live Studio wizard, page by page, with screenshots and pain points. Input for the Architect (redesign) thread. Capture-only — no Studio code changed.

Captured 2026-07-02 Docker · shared mode · :8083 Engine + KS wired Driven via Claude-in-Chrome Sample: “Account Service” (CRUD, Java 21)
How this was produced. The Studio wizard was driven live in a real browser as a working architect would. A rich CRUD project (Account + Transaction entities, REST-classified; four upstream edge contracts incl. SOAP read-by-id; four downstream contracts incl. SOAP invoke-by-id; four staging handoffs; and spec-derived rules) was loaded into the live session so that every step renders in a populated, grown-long state — including Step 3 (Entity Model) and Step 6 (Rules), which an earlier text-only pass could not reach. Screenshots below are real stills extracted from scroll-through recordings of each page. A Rich-sample coverage & method section at the end maps the sample to the capture brief and notes what was scoped out. This supersedes and corrects docs/studio-ux-current-state-audit-2026-07.md, whose Step 3 / Step 6 sections were marked “could not evaluate.”

1 Project Setup

Identity, archetype (one-way door), target profile, paths, and the Knowledge Assist toggle — all on one page.

How it’s used

Fill identity, pick an archetype up front (the page warns “changing the archetype resets later wizard state” — a genuine one-way door), optionally flip Knowledge Assist on.

First-hand pain points

  • The Output Path helper text reads “Defaults to ~/Documents/GitHub/AppBuilder/GeneratedApps” — which is not this Docker deployment’s real default. Static help that hardcodes a path is guaranteed to drift across deployments.
  • The three archetype cards read well individually, but nothing previews what Step 2+ looks like for each choice — you commit to CRUD vs Kafka before seeing either flow.
Frontend vs backend: UI-only for the help-text drift. The archetype lock-in is a real product decision (it selects the whole wizard step set), not a rendering bug.

2 Upstream Contract

Register inbound contracts. REST/OpenAPI is the only path that classifies real CRUD entities; file/CSV/XML/SOAP are captured as manifest references.

First-hand pain points

  • The structural headline: file/XML/SOAP contracts here are references only — they never feed the entity model. An architect who starts with “the mainframe files and the SOAP service” can author many valid contracts and still hit an empty Step 3, with no warning until they get there. (Confirmed in the prior pass: Step 3 says verbatim “Studio does not yet derive CRUD entities … from XML/XSD, SOAP/WSDL, or file contracts.”)
  • Saved contracts collapse into a flat “Loaded Edge Contracts” table — the right pattern (keeps many contracts scannable in ~one screen), and notably the opposite of Step 5’s always-expanded cards.
  • Two “content” fields per contract (generic sample-payload vs the type-specific field) and only the type-specific one determines READY TO EXPORT vs REFERENCE ONLY — undocumented until you save and re-read the table.
  • Re-adding a contract with the same Interface Name silently upserts it (useful!), but there’s no visible “edit” affordance on a saved row.
Frontend vs backend: backend-coupled for entity-derivation and content validation; UI-fixable for the missing edit affordance and the two-content-fields confusion.

3 Entity Model newly captured populated

Confirm the classified entities and author per-field identity roles. (The prior report could only show this empty — here it’s fully populated.)

First-hand pain points

  • Density & repetition: the page renders a full identity-role row for every field of every entity (12 rows here), and the vast majority are “No identity role” with three identical “No … behavior” lines in the Engine-behavior column. The signal (usually one persistence_id per entity) is buried in near-identical rows.
  • The “Current Engine Behavior” explanations are genuinely useful (they tell you a role is metadata-only vs ENGINE-ACTIVE) — but repeating the full paragraph on every NO-ROLE row is a lot of vertical noise.
Frontend vs backend: UI-only — collapsing / defaulting NO-ROLE rows or showing roles as a compact per-entity summary needs no manifest change. Entity derivation itself is backend.

4 Data Handoffs

Author staging tables (the only supported handoff type) with a live-generated DDL preview and entity→column mappings.

First-hand pain points

  • The DDL badge flips GENERATED FROM FIELDS → MANUAL OVERRIDE after edit/regenerate cycles with no obvious triggering action — quietly making you responsible for hand-maintaining SQL.
  • Confirmed first-hand at four handoffs: every handoff is a full always-expanded card stacked on one page — reaching the fourth table's DDL preview meant scrolling past three complete column grids. Same always-expanded failure mode as Step 5, and exactly the “past 3–4 handoffs” length the brief flagged.
Positive: “Seed mapping rows from layout fields” + auto-DDL-from-columns are exactly the “derive it, don’t make me retype it” pattern the review was asked to look for — done well.
Frontend vs backend: UI-only for the badge-flip clarity and the length; the multi-handoff generation semantics are backend.

5 Downstream Interfaces headline finding

Author outbound edge contracts (fixed-width, CSV, XML/XSD, SOAP). Unlike Step 2, cards here never collapse — every contract stays fully expanded and stacks vertically.

The first four stills below are one continuous scroll through three downstream contracts (a fifth still, further down, adds the SOAP card). Reviewing just those three required roughly 85 scroll-wheel ticks; the four upstream edge contracts on Step 2 (previous section) sit in a single flat table reviewable in ~one screen, because Step 2 collapses to a table and Step 5 never does. Comparable data, an order of magnitude apart in effort-per-contract — this is the clearest “grown-long” evidence in the app.

First-hand pain points

  • Always-expanded cards vs Step 2’s collapse-to-table — the inconsistency between two adjacent, similarly-shaped steps is the finding, not either pattern alone.
  • The same contract appears in up to three places on one page: the editable card, a “Contract Export Readiness” table lower down, and a “Saved File Contract Specs” accordion — none obviously “the one to edit.”
  • Contract type is text-only (the “Type” dropdown label) — nothing visually distinguishes a fixed-width card from an XML card at a glance.
Frontend vs backend: UI / information-architecture — collapse-to-summary and de-duplicating the triple display need no manifest change.

6 Rules & Legacy Notes corrects prior report

Field-level and cross-entity business rules, plus free-text legacy notes. The prior text-only pass (with no entities) saw only a thin textarea and concluded the page was “relatively thin.” That was wrong. Populated, it’s a rich rule-authoring surface.

First-hand pain points

  • Genuinely good: rules are pre-populated from the spec and carry SPEC-DERIVED vs MANUAL/IMPORTED provenance — you edit/remove pre-filled rows rather than starting blank.
  • Structure is a flat per-entity list; past a handful of rules per entity there’s no grouping (by field, by rule type) — it will get long the same way Steps 4/5 do.
  • No advisory/blocking distinction or conflict UI is visible here (the right rail notes “Issues & Conflicts are advisory only”) — consistent with the current soft-governance posture.
Frontend vs backend: UI-only for grouping/scaling the list; rule extraction + provenance are backend (and already working well).

7 Review Checkpoint positive pattern

A pre-export readiness dashboard: Ready/Warning/Manual counts, review posture, a compact Project Snapshot, and a bottom “Review Drawer” (manifest diff / decision history / completeness).

This is the best-designed page in the flow. Color-coded counts, a compact snapshot table, and dense detail relegated to a drawer. Noted here only as an observation — evidence that compact-summary UX is achievable inside Studio today — not as a prescribed target for the other steps. Whether and how to draw on it is entirely the Architect thread's call.
Frontend vs backend: n/a — noted as a positive reference for the redesign.

8 Export & Build

Two stages: 8a Manifest Package (Write / Validate / Assess / Download, plus a one-click pipeline) and 8b Engine Actions (Generate, then Build & Run — the latter server-disabled in shared mode).

First-hand pain points (from the prior generate run on this same pipeline)

  • Validate “pass” ≠ Generate “pass.” A content-less “reference-only” downstream SOAP contract hard-failed Validate with a FileNotFoundError, while an equally content-less upstream SOAP contract passed the same Validate — then failed at Generate with a deep WSDL-structure error. Inconsistent reference-only handling, and deep checks deferred to the very last step.
  • The errors themselves are well-designed (“Actionable Error” boxes naming the exact interface and gap) — but reaching a clean state took real SOAP/WSDL expertise the visual form never hinted at.
  • With 0 classified entities, the Engine synthesized a fallback pseudo-entity from the bounded-context name and collapsed all staging handoffs onto it — a confusing “maps to multiple staging contracts” error naming an entity the user never typed. (Resolved here by loading a real entity model.)
Frontend vs backend: backend-coupled (real WSDL/entity semantics); the UX gap — a form that accepts a placeholder WSDL with no early signal it’ll fail Generate — is a joint fix (surface backend validation earlier).

Knowledge Workspace

A separate evidence/reference-document library for Knowledge Assist, explicitly scoped away from contract ingestion.

First-hand pain points

  • Reached only after persisting KA-on via the Step-1 form — toggling the checkbox alone is client-side and /knowledge silently redirects back to Step 1 if the server session still has KA off.
  • Empty-state here by design in this capture; the accept/edit/reject suggestion loop needs a real ingested evidence document to exercise (out of scope for this pass).
Positive: the explicit “not this workspace” copy at exactly the point of ambiguity is a small, well-placed win.

Cross-cutting UI system

  • Navigation / wizard shell — the persistent left sidebar (8 numbered steps with Open/Current/Complete sub-labels) is a real strength; “where am I” is always answerable. What it does not convey: warnings/partial-fill state (a step reads “Complete” while still able to fail Engine generation) or which steps are inapplicable for the current archetype.
  • Visual / color system — functional but flat. Status pills (READY TO EXPORT, provenance tags) and the Step-7 count cards are the only places color carries real signal. Contract type is text-only everywhere; nothing lets you mentally separate a SOAP row from a CSV row at a glance (directly answering the “visual monotony” probe).
  • Cross-page consistency — strong for the shell; weak for “how do I add/edit a repeated item”: Step 2 collapses to a table + upsert-by-name (no edit button), Step 5 never collapses, Step 4 is closer to Step 5. Three steps, three flavors of the same interaction.
  • Derive-don’t-retype — “Seed mapping rows from layout fields” and auto-DDL are the good counter-examples (Steps 4/5 file contracts). The gap: XML/XSD and SOAP mapping authoring is fully manual on both upstream and downstream.

Explicit probe answers

ProbeFinding
Upstream/downstream pages grow long & undifferentiatedConfirmed, asymmetrically: Step 2 handles it well (collapse-to-table — four edge contracts in ~one screen); Step 5 does not (~85 ticks for 3 contracts, triple-redundant display). See Steps 2 & 5.
Handoff page length past 3–4 handoffsConfirmed first-hand at four handoffs — same always-expanded-card pattern as Step 5; unbounded vertical growth. See Step 4.
Entity-model page complexityConfirmed (now visible): one identity-role row per field × entity, heavily repetitive, mostly NO-ROLE. See Step 3.
Visual monotonyConfirmed — status pills are the only color signal; contract type is text-only. See Cross-cutting.
Hand-filled fields that could be derivedGood counter-examples exist (seed-from-layout, auto-DDL); the remaining gap is XML/SOAP mapping authoring (fully manual).
For the Architect thread — the biggest opportunity, deliberately left open. The largest quantified gap in the app is the Step 2 (collapse-to-table, ~one screen) vs Step 5 (always-expanded, ~85 ticks) asymmetry for comparable data, with Step 4 sharing Step 5's failure mode. This baseline stops at describing that gap — it does not prescribe a fix. The in-app patterns it happens to point at (Step 2's table, Step 7's snapshot) are offered purely as reference data points, not as the target. You are explicitly encouraged to think beyond anything Studio does today — novel information architecture, interaction models, and visual systems are all in scope, provided they respect the initiative's guardrails (frontend-first, manifest-compatible, deterministic-not-guessed defaults, phased/reversible). The best answer may look nothing like the current app.

Rich-sample coverage & method

How this sample maps to the Action-1 “build a deliberately rich sample project” checklist — what was captured first-hand, and what was deliberately scoped out (with the reason, since a gap is itself a finding per the brief).

Action-1 requirementStatusWhere / note
Upstream REST/OpenAPI, multiple endpoints✓ capturedAn Accounts/Transactions OpenAPI with multiple endpoints (POST/GET/PUT) — the only path that classifies entities (Account, Transaction). Steps 2 & 3.
Upstream fixed-width, CSV, XML/XSD, SOAP (read-by-id)✓ capturedFour edge contracts (account-status-feed, transaction-extract-csv, account-audit-xml, account-lookup-soap canonical read-by-id) in the flat Loaded Edge Contracts table. Step 2 (both new stills).
Downstream fixed-width EOD, CSV, XML/XSD, SOAP (invoke-by-id)✓ capturedFour always-expanded downstream cards incl. payment-notify-soap canonical invoke-by-id. Step 5 (four stills).
4+ staging / handoff tables✓ capturedFour staging-table handoffs (Account + transaction/payment/customer-staging) — the grown-long state. Step 4 (new still).
Several entities, fields, rules (field-check + cross-entity)✓ capturedAccount + Transaction, 6 fields each, with spec-derived allowed-values / max-length / range / pattern rules. Steps 3 & 6.
Downstream Kafka topicscoped out — with reasonKafka is a separate Studio archetype (kafka-integration, its own /kafka/* routes) that cannot coexist with the CRUD archetype — switching archetype resets the whole project. Capturing it here would have destroyed the rich CRUD sample. It warrants its own capture pass; flagged for Action-3 as a distinct surface, not a missing card on Step 5.
Exercise KA accept / edit / reject loopscoped out — with reasonThe suggestion loop needs a real ingested evidence document in the Knowledge Workspace. In this environment the browser file_upload only accepts files the user attaches in chat — a staged disk file is rejected — so the accept/edit/reject flow could not be driven end-to-end. The workspace shell itself is captured (Knowledge Workspace section); this is the one Action-1 item left un-exercised.
